    with zipfile.ZipFile(result_zip) as zf:

{"actor_role": "PI", "errors": [], "ok": true, "result": {"context": "Auto-research recording contract

Template-driven node recording:
- Use node.add as the single PI-facing node creation tool.
- parents=[] creates a root; one parent creates a child; two or more parents create a merge.
- x69z generates node_id and timestamps; omit node_id unless a stable human slug is truly needed.
- After record_node succeeds, use the returned node_id/use_in_parents as the exact parent id for child or merge nodes. Do not infer parent ids from titles.
- Custom node content belongs in fields and is validated against the chosen template.

Built-in node templates:
- generic_research: Generic Research Node (fields: title, description, note)
- kaggle_submission: Kaggle Submission (fields: intervention, public_score, previous_best, result_note, blocked_by)
- simple_ml_iteration: Simple ML Iteration (fields: improvement, score, note)

Parentage rules:
- direct_refinement: parent_id=source node, edge_type=refine, guidance=Use when the proposal preserves the same research hypothesis and changes implementation details, scope, or strength.
- debug_repair: parent_id=buggy node, edge_type=debug, guidance=Use when the proposal primarily fixes execution errors, invalid artifacts, or broken evaluation while keeping the intended idea.
- ablation: parent_id=tested node, edge_type=ablate, guidance=Use when removing or replacing a component to test whether it was necessary for the observed effect.
- replication: parent_id=tested node, edge_type=replicate, guidance=Use when repeating the same experiment under new seeds, folds, or controlled reruns to estimate variance.
- independent_branch: parent_id=None, edge_type=None, guidance=Use a root node when the proposal changes the core hypothesis, method family, or evaluation target enough that lineage would be misleading. Link it later with a decision note if it was inspired by prior work.
- merge: parent_id=primary source node, edge_type=merge, guidance=Use when combining two or more validated ideas. Set parent_id to the primary source and add merge edges from all contributing nodes.

Task status transition rules:
- Task status events are append-only; do not rewrite prior task records.
- Valid transition_type values: correction, override, progress, reopen
- Normal forward progress should use transition_type=progress.
- Moving from a terminal status (completed, failed, cancelled) back to an active status (assigned, running, blocked) is allowed when reopening or correcting research history.
- Such reactivation must use one of: correction, override, reopen
- Governed transitions must include a concrete reason and actor in by.

Context reference rules:
- Use kind:value format for every context_ref.
- Valid context_ref kinds: archive_entries.jsonl, archive_samples.jsonl, artifacts.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, edges.jsonl, file, node_patch_events.jsonl, node_review_events.jsonl, node_templates.jsonl, nodes.jsonl, note, specialist_reports.jsonl, specialist_tasks.jsonl, submissions.jsonl, task_status_events.jsonl, url
- Research refs are checked against the research store when bound.
- Exchange refs are checked against the task/report/event logs when bound.
- External refs (file, url, note) are syntax pointers; permission and existence checks belong to the harness or reviewer.

Recommended record style:
- Keep IDs short and stable, for example baseline, norm_ablation, merge_smoke, or leaderboard_probe.
- Do not repeat the project name or date in node_id/task_id/artifact_id; x69z stores created_at/updated_at timestamps at second precision.
- Use hypothesis/plan/summary fields for scientific meaning instead of encoding meaning into long IDs.
- Suggested ML shape: choose simple_ml_iteration and put the main metric in fields.score; keep raw metric tables as artifacts.
- Evidence tools are role-scoped. If artifact.record or submission.record is not visible, put known refs in artifact_refs/submission_refs or assign an experimenter/adapter to register them.

Strategy-tree cleanup descriptors:
- Use descriptors.lane for conceptual layer: main_benchmark, method_branch, negative_result, diagnostic, tool_feedback, human_review, or another concise project-specific lane.
- Use descriptors.visibility for dashboard emphasis: mainline, secondary, archived_auxiliary, collapsed, hidden, or archived.
- Use descriptors.conceptual_parent_ids as an array when the effective conceptual parent differs from append-only physical edges.
- Use descriptors.physical_parent_note to explain why physical merge edges and conceptual parentage differ.
- Use descriptors.alias for a stable human-readable name and descriptors.score_detail for compact multi-metric summaries.
- Prefer these descriptor fields over older ad hoc names such as track, intended_parent, or benchmark_context.

Custom node templates:
- Built-in templates are only defaults. Project templates can live in .x69z/node_templates/*.json and are loaded with the runtime.
- A template proposal should include template_id, fields schema, display roles, validation constraints, and intended actor roles.
- If template registration is not exposed as a normal PI tool in the current host, request a host-authorized maintainer/toolsmith flow.

Minimal record examples:
- Node: {template_id: simple_ml_iteration, fields: {improvement: 'Kaggle Titanic baseline', score: 0.818}, parents: []}
- Artifact refs: use artifact_refs: [file:results/titanic/submission.csv] until an experimenter/adapter registers artifacts.
- Submission refs: use submission_refs or assign an experimenter/adapter when submission.record is not visible.
- Task: {task_id: review_baseline, role: experimenter, target_node_id: baseline, context_refs: [nodes.jsonl:baseline]}

Node edit and review rules:
- Use node.edit for human review, PI conclusions, questions, status corrections, and effective field edits.
- Use node.edit.resolves to close PI Inbox items. Mentioning a ref in free text is only evidence and does not close the reminder.
- Use new_status for node lifecycle changes; do not patch status as a regular field.
- Use dot paths such as descriptors.lane, descriptors.visibility, descriptors.archived_reason, and descriptors.conceptual_parent_ids.
- A review-only edit records a comment without changing the node.
- A diff edit updates the effective node view append-only and must include a concise review explaining the change.
- FeedbackStore has been removed. Put human/API/evaluation results into node reviews, template fields, artifacts, or submissions.
- Minimal inbox close: {node_id: baseline, review: 'Handled review', resolves: [node_review_events.jsonl:review_id]}.
- Minimal conceptual reparent: {node_id: branch, review: 'Move in conceptual view', edits: [{path: descriptors.conceptual_parent_ids, operation: replace, value: [parent_id]}]}.

Node removal rules:
- Use node.remove for effective-view deletion; raw nodes.jsonl and edges.jsonl are not physically rewritten.
- mode=hide hides one node from default views without changing lineage.
- mode=detach removes one effective edge. If it would orphan a child, provide replacement_parent_id or promote_children_to_roots=true.
- mode=prune removes a node from the effective view. Non-leaf prune requires cascade=true with cascade_confirmed=true, replacement_parent_id, or promote_children_to_roots=true.

Host schema reload:
- If a just-added field is rejected as unexpected by MCP, reload the host MCP server or restart the host session so the latest ToolSpec schema is visible.

PI and host sub-agent boundary:
- PI owns strategy, search-tree maintenance, node reviews, and final conclusions.
- Host-native sub-agents own bounded literature search, implementation, experiment execution, result extraction, and review tasks.
- x69z records actor identity, role policy, and launch context; the host remains responsible for creating, running, and closing sub-agents.
- New tools or skills may be drafted by specialists, but activation requires PI review and, for risky capabilities, human authorization.

Prompt template maintenance rules:
Persistent prompt templates:
- PT-01 Treat prompt templates as behavioral guidance, not enforcement. Validators and hooks enforce structure; prompts make the rules visible.
- PT-02 Keep durable rules concise, specific, and grouped under stable headings. Move task-specific detail into task prompts or specialist context refs.
- PT-03 Layer context from broad to narrow: project intent, current research state, recording rules, then task-specific instructions.
- PT-04 Expose registration boundaries before the PI writes records, especially rules that allow unusual but valid actions such as reopening completed work.
- PT-05 Avoid enumerating ideation taxonomies in exploration context unless the PI is recording a node; this preserves exploratory freedom.
- PT-06 Prefer references to source records and logs over copying large content into prompts.
